title: SQL Set 08: IT Project Allocation, Bug Triage & Sprints
description: Application-development domain SQL: multi-project developers, sprint bug burndown, JDBC-ready parameterized reporting, and bench detection.

queries.title: Over-Allocated Engineers (> 100% Bandwidth)
queries.prompt: Join `engineers` and `allocations` to return `eng_name` and `total_pct` for engineers whose total `alloc_pct` across active projects exceeds 100. Order by `total_pct` DESC, `eng_name` ASC.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE engineers (eng_id INT PRIMARY KEY, eng_name TEXT); CREATE TABLE allocations (eng_id INT, proj_code TEXT, alloc_pct INT);
queries.seedSql: INSERT INTO engineers VALUES (1,'Kunal'),(2,'Tanya'),(3,'Harish'); INSERT INTO allocations VALUES (1,'HCL-API',60),(1,'HCL-UI',60),(2,'HCL-DB',100),(3,'HCL-QA',50),(3,'HCL-ML',75);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT e.eng_name, SUM(a.alloc_pct) AS total_pct FROM engineers e JOIN allocations a ON e.eng_id = a.eng_id GROUP BY e.eng_id, e.eng_name HAVING SUM(a.alloc_pct) > 100 ORDER BY total_pct DESC, e.eng_name ASC;
queries.explanation: Summing allocations per engineer and filtering `HAVING SUM(a.alloc_pct) > 100` surfaces over-committed developers.

queries.title: Bench Engineers Ready for Project Deployment
queries.prompt: Find `eng_id` and `skill` of engineers in `bench_roster` who do NOT appear in `active_pods`, ordered by `eng_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE bench_roster (eng_id INT PRIMARY KEY, skill TEXT); CREATE TABLE active_pods (pod_id INT, eng_id INT);
queries.seedSql: INSERT INTO bench_roster VALUES (10,'Java'),(11,'Spring Boot'),(12,'Python'),(13,'SQL'); INSERT INTO active_pods VALUES (1,10),(2,12);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT b.eng_id, b.skill FROM bench_roster b WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM active_pods p WHERE p.eng_id = b.eng_id) ORDER BY b.eng_id;
queries.explanation: `NOT EXISTS` cleanly locates unallocated engineers on the bench.

queries.title: Open Critical & High Bugs per Microservice
queries.prompt: For each `service_name` in `bugs` having at least 1 `'OPEN'` bug, return `service_name`, `open_critical`, and `open_high`, ordered by `service_name`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE bugs (bug_id INT PRIMARY KEY, service_name TEXT, severity TEXT, status TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT service_name, SUM(CASE WHEN severity = 'CRITICAL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_critical, SUM(CASE WHEN severity = 'HIGH' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_high FROM bugs WHERE status = 'OPEN' GROUP BY service_name ORDER BY service_name;
queries.explanation: Filtering `WHERE status = 'OPEN'` automatically drops `mail-svc` (whose only bug is `CLOSED`).

queries.title: Compensation Band Distribution
queries.prompt: Classify `dev_comp` rows into `band`: `'Senior'` (`ctc >= 1200000`), `'Mid'` (`700000 <= ctc < 1200000`), else `'GET'`. Return `band` and `cnt`, ordered by `cnt` DESC, `band` ASC.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE dev_comp (dev_id INT PRIMARY KEY, ctc INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT CASE WHEN ctc >= 1200000 THEN 'Senior' WHEN ctc >= 700000 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'GET' END AS band, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM dev_comp GROUP BY band ORDER BY cnt DESC, band ASC;
queries.explanation: `CASE WHEN` expressions in `SELECT` can be grouped by alias `band` in SQLite/PostgreSQL.

queries.title: Top 2 Distinct Story-Point Sprints per Squad
queries.prompt: Find `squad`, `sprint_no`, and `points_done` for sprints ranking in the top 2 distinct `points_done` values within each `squad`. Order by `squad` ASC, `points_done` DESC, `sprint_no` ASC.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE velocity (squad TEXT, sprint_no INT, points_done INT);
queries.solutionSql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT squad, sprint_no, points_done, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY squad ORDER BY points_done DESC) AS dr FROM velocity) SELECT squad, sprint_no, points_done FROM ranked WHERE dr <= 2 ORDER BY squad ASC, points_done DESC, sprint_no ASC;
queries.explanation: `DENSE_RANK()` ensures both tied 42-point sprints share rank 1 and the 34-point sprint gets rank 2.
